PROGRAMS: DSWD AICS (Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation
DESCRIPTION: acts as a social safety net for individuals and families facing unexpected life transitions or emergencies.
BENEFICIARIES: Benificiaries are anyone in a "crisis situation," such as those dealing with a sudden death in the family, a medical emergency, or being stranded
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Families with sudden death (burial needs)
Patients needing urgent medical help
Stranded individuals (no money to go home)
Families in sudden crisis (fire, accident, etc.)
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Financial assistance for emergencies (medical, burial, transportation) / Food and basic necessities / Temporary shelter or travel support / Immediate crisis intervention

DESCRIPTION: focuses on long-term economic empowerment rather than immediate relief. t offers two tracks: the Micro-enterprise Development track (providing seed capital to start a small business) and the Employment Facilitation track (providing skills training and job placement)
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries are primarily poor, vulnerable, and marginalized households, often including those under the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps).
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Poor and vulnerable households
4Ps beneficiaries
Families needing long-term income support
Individuals who want to start or grow a business
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Seed capital for small businesses / Livelihood starter kits / Skills training for entrepreneurship / Job placement assistance

DESCRIPTION: is a nutrition-focused initiative that provides hot meals and milk to children to combat undernutrition. As of 2026, the program has expanded its duration to 180 feeding days
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries are children aged two to five years old enrolled in Child Development Centers (CDCs) and Supervised Neighborhood Playgroups (SNPs).
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Children 2–5 years old
Enrolled in daycare / child development centers
Undernourished or at risk of malnutrition
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Daily nutritious hot meals / Milk supplementation / Nutrition support for child development / Monitoring of children’s health and growth

PROGRAMS: DOLE TUPAD (Tulong Panghanapbuhay sa Ating Disadvantaged/Displaced Workers)
DESCRIPTION: is a community-based emergency employment program. It provides short-term manual labor (usually 10 to 30 days) in exchange for a daily wage based on the regional minimum.
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries are displaced, underemployed, or seasonal informal workers, and the list has recently expanded to include indigenous peoples and guardians of child laborers.
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Displaced workers (lost jobs)
Underemployed workers (not enough income)
Informal workers (vendors, drivers, laborers)
Seasonal workers (farmers, fishers)
Indigenous peoples
Guardians of child laborers
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Short-term employment (10–30 days) / Daily wages based on minimum wage / Emergency income support / Basic PPEs while working (in some cases)

DESCRIPTION: also known as the Kabuhayan Program, provides grant assistance for the purchase of raw materials, tools, and equipment for starting or enhancing a small business. Unlike TUPAD, which is a wage-for-work program, DILP provides the "starter kits" or capital for entrepreneurship.
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries include self-employed workers, marginalized farmers, fishers, and PWDs.
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Unemployed individuals
Small vendors / low-income self-employed
Solo parents needing extra income
PWDs who can run small businesses
Farmers and fishers (no income in off-season)
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Livelihood starter kits (tools, equipment, raw materials) / Capital assistance for small businesses / Support for self-employment / Capacity-building for entrepreneurs

PROGRAMS: TESDA STEP (Special Training for Employment Program)
DESCRIPTION: is a community-based specialty training program that focuses on "entrepreneurial, self-employment, and service-oriented" skills. Students receive free training, a starter tool kit for their trade, and a daily allowance.
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries are primarily residents of low-income communities who have not had prior formal or vocational training.
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Out-of-school youth (15–30)
High school graduates not in college
Stay-at-home parents
Adults with no skills
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Free technical/vocational training / Starter tool kits / Daily training allowance / Skills for self-employment

PROGRAMS: TESDA TWSP (Training for Work Scholarship Program)
DESCRIPTION: is designed to meet the specific "skills gaps" of high-demand industries like IT-BPM, construction, and tourism. It aims to make students immediately employable by partnering with industry providers.
BENEFICIARIES: Beneficiaries are individuals at least 18 years old who are looking for specific certifications to qualify for existing job vacancies in priority sectors.
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Job seekers (18+)
People with skills but no certificate
Those targeting BPO, construction, tourism
Returning OFWs
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Free industry-relevant training (IT, construction, tourism, etc.) / Certification for employment / Assessment and training costs covered / Increased employability for in-demand jobs

PROGRAMS: DOH MAIFIP (Medical Assistance to Indigent and Financially-Incapacitated Patients)
DESCRIPTION: Is a program that covers the medical and hospitalization costs of patients who cannot afford their bills in government hospitals. It works by providing a budget to public health facilities to "subsidize" the treatment of those in need.
BENEFICIARIES: The beneficiaries are patients classified as indigent or those who, while not strictly "poor," are "financially incapacitated" due to catastrophic medical expenses.
SPECIFIC BENEFACTORS:
Low-income or indigent patients
Families with emergency medical expenses
Seniors needing maintenance medicine
PWDs with medical needs
BASIC NEEDS/HELP: Financial assistance for hospital bills / Subsidy for medical treatments / Support for medicines and procedures / Access to healthcare for indigent patients
